title: Base change of proper flat dualizing complexes on polynomial models
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to S$ a proper, flat morphism of finite presentation [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $K_f=f^!\mathcal O_S$, with its adjunction trace and its normalized polynomial-chart comparisons, be as in [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model]. The diagonal-class normalization of these comparisons is specified in [lem-sfb-proper-polynomial-comparison-class-normalization]. Let $a:S'\to S$ be any morphism of schemes. Put $X'=X\times_SS'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projection $b:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$; then $f'$ is again proper, flat and of finite presentation. Let $\beta_a:Lb^*K_f\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{f'}$ be the trace-pair base-change isomorphism of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality]. It is read on Zariski derived quasi-coherent modules through that node's agreement with $f^!$, and $Lb^*$ is [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}(V)$ be affine opens. Let $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ be a polynomial presentation and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset a^{-1}(V)$ an affine open. Put $P'=P\otimes_RR'$ and $B'=B\otimes_RR'$, so that $U'=\operatorname{Spec}B'=U\times_VV'\subset X'$. Then $B[0]$ is a perfect $P$-complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and $\operatorname{Tor}^P_i(B,P')=0$ for $i>0$. Interpret $K_f|_U$ and $K_{f'}|_{U'}$ through [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] and identify them with their polynomial models. Then $\beta_a|_{U'}$ is the evaluation-counit coinduction base-change isomorphism of [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-base-change]:
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega^n_{P/R})[n]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_BB'\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{P'}(B',\Omega^n_{P'/R'})[n].$$
Here $\Omega^n_{P/R}\otimes_RR'=\Omega^n_{P'/R'}$ sends $dt_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dt_n$ to $dt_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dt_n$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Derived Hom is derived coinduction with its natural $B$-action [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-trf-derived-coinduction]. These local descriptions commute with restriction to smaller affine opens and with the normalized ordered polynomial-refinement comparisons on both sides. They also respect identity and composition of base changes. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ or $S'$ and no flatness of $a$ is assumed.

proof.text: Base change preserves properness, flatness and finite presentation, by the three permanence statements cited here. Thus the same proper duality and polynomial-model theorems apply to $f'$. The affine criteria applied to $U/V$ give $R\to B$ flat and finitely presented. Apply [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-dual-properties] with its $A=B$ to this very presentation $P\twoheadrightarrow B$. It says $B[0]$ is perfect over $P$, without a Noetherian hypothesis. This does not follow by applying the Noetherian polynomial-quotient lemma directly to $R$.

Choose a free $P$-resolution $F_\bullet\to B$. The monomial description of $P$ makes each free $P$-module free over $R$, so the same augmented complex is a free $R$-resolution of $B$. Degreewise the balanced-tensor isomorphism is
$$F_j\otimes_P(P\otimes_RR')\longrightarrow F_j\otimes_RR',\quad z\otimes(p\otimes r')\longmapsto pz\otimes r',$$
with inverse $z\otimes r'\mapsto z\otimes(1\otimes r')$; these maps commute with differentials and augmentations. Hence the resolution definition of Tor identifies $\operatorname{Tor}_i^P(B,P')$ with $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(B,R')$. The base-flat polynomial Tor-bound node, applied to the $R$-flat $P$-module $B$, explicitly says the latter vanishes for $i>0$. Thus the augmented tensor complex resolves $B'$, and $B\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'\simeq B'[0]$. The same argument works with $R$ replaced by any base ring and any base-flat polynomial quotient, as used below.

source.place: more-algebra.tex Tag 0661 (lemma-base-change-comparison), free-resolution computation; Tag 068X (lemma-perfect-over-polynomial-ring), base-flat input.

proof.text:
Write $L=\Omega^n_{P/R}[n]$ and $C=C_B^P(L)$. Perfect coinduction base change, with $(A,B,A',N)=(P,B,P',L)$, gives its evaluation-counit mate
$$c:C\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{B'}^{P'}(L\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P').$$
All Tor and perfectness hypotheses were verified in steps 1--2. Polynomial differentials have the ordered basis $dt_i$; [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis] makes their top exterior power free of rank one on the ordered wedge. Their differential base-change map sends $dt_i\otimes1$ to $dt_i$; on the top exterior basis it sends $dt_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dt_n$ to the same wedge. Thus $L\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'=\Omega^n_{P'/R'}[n]$: this coefficient is a shifted free rank-one module, so ordinary tensor computes its derived tensor. Under affine derived pullback the source is the restriction of $Lb^*K_f$. The exchange lemma also identifies the underlying finite-projective Hom map as $(h\otimes u)(z\otimes v)=uv(h(z)\otimes1)$, with its actual $B'$-action.

proof.text: Use the arbitrary-ring graph-class theorem with the flat finitely presented algebra $B/R$ established in step 1. It supplies the specific class $\xi_P$ and its scalar-extension equality for $c$ from step 3, on $Q=B\otimes_RB\to Q'=B'\otimes_{R'}B'$. Thus $c$ carries the derived pullback of $\xi_P$ to $\xi_{P'}$, with the actual evaluation-counit normalization, not just the span of a generator. The new comparison-normalization theorem identifies both $(C,\xi_P)$ and $(C',\xi_{P'})$ with the restrictions of the intrinsic pairs under the specified canonical chart comparisons. It states both class equations explicitly. All its hypotheses hold for $f,f'$ by step 1. This uses a purely affine algebra scalar-compatibility lemma, followed by a single-base geometric normalization lemma; neither identifies the map $\beta_a$.

source.place: Agent arbitrary-ring scalar clause of Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian), with Tag 0E2F (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing), Tags 0A70/0A71 (lemma-right-adjoint, lemma-RHom-ext), and ordered volume convention of Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic). Exact normalized-class compatibility is an agent enhancement of the generator claim of 0E2F.

proof.text: Relate the prescribed trace comparison to these classes before using rigidity. Restrict first over the affine bases $V,V'$, retaining the entire proper schemes $X_V,X_{V'}$. The space-duality theorem and its scheme agreement identify their trace pairs with the right-adjoint images of $\mathcal O_V,\mathcal O_{V'}$. The affine proper-flat adjoint-base-change theorem constructs the adjoint exchange by pulling the counit and says it preserves that counit. Trace-pair uniqueness therefore identifies it with the restriction of the given $\beta_a$. Now [lem-sfb-proper-adjoint-diagonal-pair] applies: $V,V'$ are qcqs, and the two morphisms are proper flat of finite presentation. Its explicit base-change clause says this right-adjoint exchange preserves the induced diagonal classes. The affine-base clause of [lem-sfb-proper-polynomial-comparison-class-normalization] identifies the intrinsic classes with exactly these adjoint classes, under the trace-preserving identifications. Its chart clause carries their restrictions to $\xi_P$ and the primed class. Restrict the resulting class-preserving comparison further to $U'$. No global qcqs hypothesis on $S$ or $S'$ has been inserted, and no right adjoint for the nonproper $U/V$ has been used.

The pullback pair on $U'/V'$ is a supplied coherent relative dualizing pair by [lem-sfb-relative-dualizing-pair-base-change]. Its target polynomial pair and the class equations for the canonical chart comparisons are supplied by [lem-sfb-proper-polynomial-comparison-class-normalization]. Step 4 proves that $c$ preserves their classes, and step 5 proves that the prescribed $\beta_a|_{U'}$ does too. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-dualizing-pair-open-rigidity] on $U'/V'$: there is exactly one class-preserving isomorphism. It equates these two maps. The affine equivalence is fully faithful, so this is the asserted equality of morphisms in $D(B')$, with the evaluation-counit coinduction base-change map of step 3 and precisely the displayed coefficient-line identification.

Use the class-normalized chart identifications of [lem-sfb-proper-polynomial-comparison-class-normalization] throughout. For a one-variable refinement choose the lift $u\in P$ of its additional coordinate image. Its normalized contraction sends $\operatorname{dual}(t-u)\otimes d(t-u)$ to $1$. After any scalar extension it sends $\operatorname{dual}(t-u')\otimes d(t-u')$ to the same $1$; perfect coinduction base change preserves exactly these Koszul evaluations. Ordered tensoring retains the degree signs $(-1)^{ij}$ because a ring map sends each integer sign to itself. Thus the refinement square commutes, with the ordered signs, for one coordinate and by composition for every ordered refinement. For a principal affine restriction, localizing the finite-projective Hom formula in step 3 gives the same formula on each path: $uv(h(z)\otimes1)$ simply acquires the indicated denominators. The polynomial-model theorem supplies these restriction and refinement comparisons and their cocycles; the normalization theorem explicitly identifies its same canonical comparisons with the class-normalized ones. For arbitrary smaller affine opens, use principal subopens and a common polynomial refinement on them; pair rigidity identifies the two maps after restriction, hence identifies the pair comparisons on the smaller open itself. This last use of uniqueness avoids claiming that arbitrary derived morphisms are a Zariski sheaf.

source.place: Tags 0BZI and 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), ordered polynomial refinements; duality.tex Tag 0E2W, rigidity on every open.

proof.text: For an identity base change, the counit mate is the identity by the identity comparison in the coinduction-base-change theorem. For a tower $R\to R'\to R''$, $B'$ is again flat over $R'$; step 2 verifies all the successive Tor conditions, and that theorem equates direct and successive maps under the tensor associators. They therefore give the identity and composition laws for the chart descriptions. The space trace-pair theorem gives the same laws for the prescribed global maps, so the identification in step 6 respects them. If $n=0$, the ordered volume is $1\in P=R$ and the graph Koszul complex is the empty tensor with identity evaluation. If $B=0$ or $R'=0$, the pertinent target is the zero derived category and every displayed equality is its unique map. None of the arguments assumes the base rings are nonzero or Noetherian or that $R\to R'$ is flat.
